properties.headline: Severe Thunderstorm Warning issued October 13 at 7:02PM CDT until October 13 at 8:15PM CDT by NWS Lubbock TX
properties.description:
SVRLUB

The National Weather Service in Lubbock Texas has issued a

* Severe Thunderstorm Warning for...
Northeastern Dickens County in northwestern Texas...
Northwestern King County in northwestern Texas...
Southeastern Motley County in northwestern Texas...
Cottle County in northwestern Texas...

* Until 815 PM CDT.

* At 702 PM CDT, severe thunderstorms were located along a line
extending from 11 miles northwest of Delwin to 10 miles southeast
of Afton, moving northeast at 45 mph.

HAZARD...Ping pong ball size hail and 60 mph wind gusts.

SOURCE...Radar indicated.

IMPACT...People and animals outdoors will be injured. Expect hail
damage to roofs, siding, windows, and vehicles. Expect
wind damage to roofs, siding, and trees.

* Locations impacted include...
Paducah, Grow, Dumont, Finney, Delwin, Chalk, Swearingen, and
Hackberry.
properties.instruction:
For your protection move to an interior room on the lowest floor of a
building.

properties.headline: Severe Thunderstorm Warning issued October 13 at 7:00PM CDT until October 13 at 7:30PM CDT by NWS Kansas City/Pleasant Hill MO
properties.description:
At 700 PM CDT, severe thunderstorms were located along a line from
near Lansing to 8 miles west of Linwood, or along a line from near
Lansing to 11 miles southwest of Tonganoxie, moving east at 30 mph.

HAZARD...70 mph wind gusts and quarter size hail.

SOURCE...Radar indicated. This storm has a history of 60 to 70 MPH
winds.

IMPACT...Hail damage to vehicles is expected. Expect considerable
tree damage. Wind damage is also likely to mobile homes,
roofs, and outbuildings.

Locations impacted include...
Overland Park, Olathe, Shawnee, Lenexa, Leawood, Prairie Village,
Merriam, Mission, Bonner Springs, De Soto, Parkville, Tonganoxie,
Basehor, Edwardsville, Fairway, Mission Hills, Riverside, Westwood
and Lake Quivira.
properties.instruction:
Anyone outdoors should move to shelter inside a well-built structure
and stay away from windows. These storms are capable of producing
widespread damaging winds and large hail.

properties.description:
At 700 PM CDT, a severe thunderstorm was located 6 miles northwest of
Higgins, or 8 miles southeast of Lipscomb, moving northeast at 35
mph.

HAZARD...Ping pong ball size hail and 60 mph wind gusts.

SOURCE...Radar indicated.

IMPACT...Minor damage to roofs, siding, and trees is possible.
People and animals outdoors will be injured. Expect hail
damage to roofs, siding, windows, and vehicles.

Locations impacted include...
Lipscomb, Canadian, Higgins, Glazier, and Lake Marvin.
properties.instruction:
For your protection move to an interior room on the lowest floor of a
building.

Continuous cloud to ground lightning is occurring with this storm.
Move indoors immediately. Lightning is one of nature's leading
killers. Remember, if you can hear thunder, you are close enough to
be struck by lightning.

Torrential rainfall is occurring with this storm, and may lead to
flash flooding. Do not drive your vehicle through flooded roadways.

properties.headline: Severe Thunderstorm Warning issued October 13 at 6:56PM CDT until October 13 at 8:00PM CDT by NWS Amarillo TX
properties.description:
SVRAMA

The National Weather Service in Amarillo has issued a

* Severe Thunderstorm Warning for...
Wheeler County in the Panhandle of Texas...
Southeastern Gray County in the Panhandle of Texas...
Collingsworth County in the Panhandle of Texas...
South central Hemphill County in the Panhandle of Texas...
Donley County in the Panhandle of Texas...

* Until 800 PM CDT.

* At 654 PM CDT, a cluster of severe thunderstorms were located in
southern Donley and Collingsworth County and most of Hall County.
Storms are tracking north northeast 40 mph.

HAZARD...60 mph wind gusts and quarter size hail.

SOURCE...Radar indicated.

IMPACT...Minor damage to roofs, siding, and trees is possible.
Hail damage to vehicles is expected.

* Locations impacted include...
Wellington, Clarendon, Shamrock, Briscoe, Wheeler, Mclean, Hedley,
Dodson, Lutie, Lelia Lake, New Mobeetie, Twitty, Allison, Lela,
Quail, Samnorwood, Kellerville, Dozier, and Mobeetie.
properties.instruction:
For your protection move to an interior room on the lowest floor of a
building.

Large hail, damaging wind, and continuous cloud to ground lightning
are occurring with these storms. Move indoors immediately. Lightning
is one of nature's leading killers. Remember, if you can hear
thunder, you are close enough to be struck by lightning.

Torrential rainfall is occurring with these storms, and may lead to
flash flooding. Do not drive your vehicle through flooded roadways.

thunderstorms. This  will cause urban and small stream flooding.

- Additional rainfall amounts of 0.5 to 1.5 inches are expected
over the area. This additional rain will result in minor
flooding.

Comanche County in south central Kansas...
Southeastern Clark County in southwestern Kansas...

properties.areaDesc: Ventura County Beaches; Malibu Coast; Los Angeles County Beaches
properties.headline: Beach Hazards Statement issued October 13 at 4:20PM PDT until October 15 at 2:00PM PDT by NWS Los Angeles/Oxnard CA
properties.description:
* WHAT...Minor tidal overflow during times of high tides,
dangerous rip currents, and elevated surf.

* WHERE...Ventura County Beaches, Malibu Coast and Los Angeles
County Beaches.

* WHEN...Through Thursday afternoon.

* IMPACTS...Minor flooding of sea water is likely around high
tide at low-lying beach and harbor areas that is uncommon with
normal tidal ranges. Enhanced beach erosion is possible. The
risk for significant damage is very low. There is an increased
risk of ocean drowning. Rip currents can pull swimmers and
surfers out to sea. Waves can wash people off beaches and
rocks, and capsize small boats nearshore.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...Minor tidal overflow during morning high
tides of 6.5 to 7.0 feet.
properties.instruction:
Take the necessary actions to protect flood-prone property. Do
NOT drive around barricades or through water of unknown depth.

Remain out of the water due to hazardous swimming conditions, or
stay near occupied lifeguard towers. Rock jetties can be deadly
in such conditions, stay off the rocks.

properties.areaDesc: San Luis Obispo County Mountains; Santa Barbara County Interior Mountains
properties.headline: Fire Weather Watch issued October 13 at 2:38PM PDT until October 16 at 6:00PM PDT by NWS Los Angeles/Oxnard CA
properties.description:
***CORRECTED HEADLINE FOR SANTA BARBARA AND SAN LUIS OBISPO
COUNTIES***

...HIGH RISK FOR EXTREME FIRE BEHAVIOR WITH ANY NEW FIRE STARTS
THURSDAY THROUGH FRIDAY DUE TO MODERATE TO LOCALLY STRONG SANTA
ANA WINDS AND LOW RELATIVE HUMIDITY...

.Moderate to locally strong Santa Ana winds will quickly develop
on Thursday, peak Thursday afternoon through Friday afternoon,
then weaken through the weekend. Meanwhile, dry air will settle
over the region and dry out any helpful effects of the recent
rains. The previous Fire Weather Watches were upgraded to Red
Flag Warnings. Some of the windiest areas may see Red Flag
conditions linger into Saturday. As the winds expand Thursday
Night into Friday, Red Flag conditions may form over the interior
mountains of Santa Barbara and San Luis Obispo Counties on
Friday, where a Fire Weather Watch is now in effect.

* AFFECTED AREA...San Luis Obispo County Mountains and Santa
Barbara County Interior Mountains.

* TIMING...From Friday morning through Friday afternoon.

* WINDS...East 15 to 25 mph with gusts up to 40 mph.

* RELATIVE HUMIDITY...Minimums of 8 to 20 percent common.

* IMPACTS...If fire ignition occurs, conditions are favorable
for extreme fire behavior which would threaten life and
property.
properties.instruction:
A Fire Weather Watch means that critical fire weather conditions
are likely to occur in the coming days. Residents near wildland
interfaces should prepare now on what to do if a wildfire breaks
out. See readyforwildfire.org and wildfirerisk.org for
information.

Pacific Coast and through the San Francisco Bay, respectively.

An active trough to the north is projected to drift southward and
move over the territory by Thursday night. Widespread showers may
be heavy and persistent at times with the possibility of thunderstorms.
Landslides will also be possible along steep mountainous terrain.
Impacts could begin as early as Thursday and are expected to
persist through the weekend. While there is still uncertainty in
the exact magnitude and duration of rainfall, plan now for wet
conditions that could persist through at least Sunday.

internet page (www.weather.gov/ppg), local media, social media,
and our NOAA Radio broadcasts.

properties.headline: Air Quality Alert issued October 13 at 2:33PM CDT by NWS Birmingham AL
properties.description:
AQABMX

The Alabama Department of Environmental Management, ADEM, has issued
an Air Quality Alert for Jefferson and Shelby Counties for
Wednesday, October 14.

Under Code Orange conditions, ground level ozone concentrations are
expected to reach levels that are unhealthy for sensitive groups.
Children and people with asthma are individuals most at risk under
these expected conditions.

ADEM recommends the following actions during an air quality alert
for ozone:

Conserve electricity and set your air conditioner at a higher
temperature.

Limit driving and combine errands.

Use the bus or car pool to work.

Avoid use of gasoline powered lawn and garden equipment.

Refuel cars and trucks after 6 PM.

Limit engine idling.

Use household, workshop, and garden chemicals in ways that keep
evaporation to a minimum, or try to avoid them when poor air quality
is forecast.

If breathing becomes difficult, move indoors.

For more information on what to do on an air quality alert day,
visit the Environmental Protection Agency website at airnow.gov
properties.note: Non-Weather Emergency Message. Not sent to IPAWS.

properties.headline: Flood Watch issued October 13 at 10:57AM AKDT until October 16 at 1:00PM AKDT by NWS Juneau AK
properties.description:
A stronger atmospheric river is expected to move over the panhandle
beginning early Thursday morning and continuing through at least
Friday morning. Multiple waves moving up will bring persistent
moderate to heavy rain for much of the southern half of the
panhandle. Past early Friday morning, additional periods of heavy
rain are possible, but confidence is moderate to low at this time.
Prolonged periods of moderate to heavy rain will produce significant
river rises with the potential for at least minor flooding.

* WHAT...Flooding caused by excessive rainfall is possible.

* WHERE...The following area, Southern Inner Channels. This includes
the cities of Ketchikan And Metlakatla.

* WHEN...From Thursday afternoon through Friday afternoon.

* IMPACTS...Excessive runoff may result in flooding of rivers,
creeks, streams, other low-lying areas and flood-prone locations.
Street flooding and flooding of creeks and rivers are possible.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- Rain totals between early Thursday morning and late Friday
morning for the Ketchikan and Metlakatla area are currently
expected around 4 to 6 inches, with higher rain totals favoring
southern facing mountainsides. Highest rain rates are currently
expected during the late morning through evening timeframe on
Thursday, where rates could exceed 0.3 inches per hour.

If the additional heavy rain moves into the southern panhandle
late Friday morning and continue through Friday afternoon, up to
an additional 1.5 inches is possible. The chances of this to
occur are around 30% at this time.
properties.instruction:
Stay tuned to further developments by listening to your local radio,
television, or NOAA Weather Radio for further information.

You should monitor later forecasts and be alert for possible Flood
Warnings. Those living in areas prone to flooding should be prepared
to take action should flooding develop.

properties.description:

move toward Southeast Alaska, bringing widespread moderate to heavy
rainfall. Strong winds are also expected for coastal and southern
panhandle communities. While the exact timing and impacts of the

developing situation and update our forecast.

* WHAT...Minor flooding is occurring and minor flooding is forecast.

* WHERE...Congaree River at Congaree River at Congaree NP Near
Gadsden.

* WHEN...Until late Thursday night.

* IMPACTS...At 15.0 feet, Flooding begins in the Congaree National
Park. This will begin to produce flooding of portions of the lower
boardwalk. At 17.0 feet, The access road to the Sandy Run
subdivision becomes flooded. The lower boardwalk in the Congaree

properties.areaDesc: Guam, GU; Rota, MP; Saipan, MP; Tinian, MP
properties.headline: Hydrologic Outlook issued October 13 at 5:31PM ChST by NWS Tiyan GU
properties.description:
ESFGUM

This Hydrologic Outlook is for Guam, Rota, Tinian, and Saipan.

Invest 96W is still a broad, disorganized disturbance located about
300 miles north of Kosrae. Ensemble model guidance continues to show
a passage anywhere between south of Guam to north of Saipan as a
tropical storm or typhoon. Uncertainty is still high regarding
timing, location, and intensity, but the potential for locally heavy
rainfall and flooding continues to increase approaching this weekend.

This is expected to produce 5 to 8 inches of rainfall between
Saturday and Monday, with localized amounts up to 12 inches possible.

As showers are likely to persist, consistent rainfall is likely to
saturate the soils enough to increase chance for mudslides.

Residents on these islands need to closely monitor this developing
situation as flood watches, advisories and flash flood warnings could
be issued later this weekend.

If living near streams and rivers, prepare to move items away from
stream and river banks. Make sure storm drains nearby are not
clogged, especially If living at low-lying areas.

NWSheadline: INCREASING POTENTIAL FOR HEAVY RAINFALL AND FLOODING THIS WEEKEND FOR THE MARIANAS

properties.areaDesc: Pohnpei Coastal Waters; Kosrae Coastal Waters
properties.headline: Special Weather Statement issued October 13 at 1:49PM ChST by NWS Tiyan GU
properties.description:
Invest 96W is currently rated as "Medium" by the Joint Typhoon
Warning Center, meaning tropical cyclone development is likely, but
beyond 24 hours. It's currently located west of Ujae near 9.3N
164.4E. It continues to slowly organize and strengthen north of
Kosrae/east-northest of Pohnpei.

Inflow into the developing disturbance will allow for locally heavy
rainfall to develop, with over 1 inch per hour rain rates probable
from time to time. Rainfall totals will likely be 2 to 5 inches
tonight through Thursday, with locally higher amounts possible.
Winds will also increase as 96W strengthens, and at least isolated
wind gusts to 30 knots are possible with any heavy shower or
thunderstorm that develops.

Gusty winds and elevated, choppy seas will make marine conditions
difficult. Residents may need to reconsider plans for inter-island
boating as the week continues. Also keep up to date with the latest
information from your local emergency management agency.
